account: Carscoops reports that the Westchester County Police Department, New York, used technology provided by Rekor. It examined the driving patterns of anyone passing its 480 license-plate-reader cameras over a two-year period. It determined that David Zayas had made several trips along routes typically used by drug traffickers and turned around quickly to go home. The Star's AFP Relaxnews item adds that police took an interest in a vehicle registered to Zayas in March 2022. On 10 March 2022 Zayas was driving a gray Chevrolet in Scarsdale. Officers pulled him over and searched the car. Carscoops reports that they found crack cocaine, cash and a pistol. Forbes reported that the search found 112 grams of crack cocaine, a semiautomatic pistol and $34,000 in cash. On 10 March 2023 the defense filed a motion to suppress the evidence from the location-data searches. The court never decided it. The federal docket shows that Zayas pleaded guilty on 28 June 2023. Forbes reported the case on 17 July 2023, and Carscoops followed on 18 July 2023, drawing on Forbes. Carscoops quotes ACLU lawyer Brett Max Kaufman and defense attorney Ben Gold, who criticized the surveillance. The OECD Monitor summary says that the system analyzed billions of plate records, and it lists harms to rights and to the public interest. On 24 January 2024 Zayas received 48 months, with a $34,000 forfeiture. A presidential commutation filed on 17 January 2025 ended his prison term on 16 May 2025. The conviction and three years of supervised release stand.

ai_role.statement: Per the defense motion, Westchester's Real Time Crime Center ran an Interdiction Analysis report in Rekor Scout over more than 1.6 billion plate records. Per a prosecutor filing cited by Forbes, it showed nine trips from Massachusetts between October 2020 and August 2021 on known trafficking routes with short stays. That flag opened the investigation and marked the car for interdiction. Officers then made the stop, questioned him and used a dog before the search, and the conviction rested on what they found. No source gives an accuracy figure or a count of other drivers flagged, and the court never decided the March 2023 motion that challenged the search of plate data.

fields.account: Carscoops reports that the Westchester County Police Department, New York, used technology provided by Rekor. It examined the driving patterns of anyone passing its 480 license-plate-reader cameras over a two-year period. It determined that David Zayas had made several trips along routes typically used by drug traffickers and turned around quickly to go home. The Star's AFP Relaxnews item adds that police took an interest in a vehicle registered to Zayas in March 2022. On 10 March 2022 Zayas was driving a gray Chevrolet in Scarsdale. Officers pulled him over and searched the car. Carscoops reports that they found crack cocaine, cash and a pistol. Forbes reported that the search found 112 grams of crack cocaine, a semiautomatic pistol and $34,000 in cash. On 10 March 2023 the defense filed a motion to suppress the evidence from the location-data searches. The court never decided it. The federal docket shows that Zayas pleaded guilty on 28 June 2023. Forbes reported the case on 17 July 2023, and Carscoops followed on 18 July 2023, drawing on Forbes. Carscoops quotes ACLU lawyer Brett Max Kaufman and defense attorney Ben Gold, who criticized the surveillance. The OECD Monitor summary says that the system analyzed billions of plate records, and it lists harms to rights and to the public interest. On 24 January 2024 Zayas received 48 months, with a $34,000 forfeiture. A presidential commutation filed on 17 January 2025 ended his prison term on 16 May 2025. The conviction and three years of supervised release stand.

purpose: Carscoops describes Rekor's Public Safety Network as aggregating vehicle location data from its customers so that police can examine driving patterns. Flagging a pattern associated with drug trafficking for a stop is the function that the network was built for.

ratings.reason: The stop removed 112 grams of crack cocaine and a semiautomatic pistol from a driver who, per a prosecutor filing that Forbes cites, had made nine trafficking-pattern trips. He pleaded guilty, received 48 months and agreed to a $34,000 forfeiture, per the court docket. The sentence was later commuted, and no source measures any effect on drug supply or violence.
